# Results — Study 99 (Safety-Net) on the real total-return tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — hold SPY long,
track the running peak of the close, and **exit to cash (earning 0%) the day the close
falls more than X% below that peak**; stay out for a **21-trading-day cooldown**, then
re-enter and reset the peak. Act one day after the trigger (drawdown known at close *t* →
position at *t+1*), charge **5 bps** per switch. Run on the **total-return** SPY tape and
pinned against (a) buy-and-hold and (b) a **matched random-exit control** that holds the
same total time in cash, in runs of the same lengths, at random dates. We sweep
**X = 5 / 10 / 15 / 20%**. As-of **2026-06-12**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold
the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY (total return) | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-12 | 8,400 | `eb1569cc9e97` |

## The X-sweep — net of 5 bps/switch, 21-day cooldown

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Time in mkt | Switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Buy & hold** | **10.82%** | 18.6% | 0.646 | −55.2% | 100% | 0 |
| Trailing stop **5%** | 6.05% | 12.6% | 0.530 | −48.0% | 76% | 195 |
| Trailing stop **10%** | 10.80% | 15.2% | **0.752** | **−43.9%** | 92% | 63 |
| Trailing stop **15%** | 10.85% | 16.2% | 0.719 | −46.7% | 96% | 35 |
| Trailing stop **20%** | 10.05% | 16.9% | 0.650 | −54.7% | 98% | 19 |

## The decisive numbers — per threshold

| X | Sharpe − B&H | Beats matched random-exit coin? | HAC *t* (stop − B&H daily ret) | CAGR gap vs B&H | Drawdown cut |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **5%** | **−0.116** | **93 / 200 (46%)** — loses to its own coin | **−2.66** | **−4.77 pts/yr** | +7.1 pts |
| **10%** | +0.106 | **200 / 200 (100%)** | −0.39 | **−0.02 pts/yr** | **+11.3 pts** |
| **15%** | +0.073 | **200 / 200 (100%)** | −0.29 | +0.03 pts/yr | +8.5 pts |
| **20%** | +0.004 | 156 / 200 (78%) | −1.06 | −0.77 pts/yr | +0.5 pts |

## How to read it — exactly Kaminski & Lo (2014)

- **No threshold beats buy-and-hold on *return*.** The best case (15%) edges it by a
  rounding-error **+0.03 pts/yr**; the headline 10% stop *matches* it (−0.02 pts/yr) and
  the tight 5% stop **bleeds 4.77 pts/yr** to whipsaw. The daily-return difference never
  clears the inference bar: HAC *t* runs **−2.66 (5%) to −0.39 (10%)** — i.e. zero or
  *negative*, never a significant positive edge. → Signal **WEAK** (it does not out-earn
  the market; the Sharpe gain at 10–15% is lower beta — less time and less vol — not skill).
- **The drawdown cut is real but entirely depends on X.** A 10% stop cuts max drawdown by
  **11.3 pts** (−43.9% vs −55.2%); a 20% stop cuts almost nothing (**+0.5 pts**); a 5% stop
  cuts 7 pts but destroys return. → 3rd axis **MIXED** — protection is genuine only in a
  middle band, and a badly-chosen X hurts.
- **The *timing* carries information — but only at the right X.** The 10% and 15% stops
  beat the exposure-matched random-exit coin **100% of the time** on Sharpe: drawdown-from-peak
  exits land in better spots than random in/out of equal duration. But the 5% stop **loses to
  random (46%)** — too tight, it fires on noise. The signal exists, conditionally; it does not
  pay. → Tradability **MIRAGE** for the "improves returns" claim.

## Synthetic controls (machinery proof, `run_synthetic_demo.py`)

| Tape | Stop Sharpe | B&H Sharpe | Expected | Result |
|---|--:|--:|---|---|
| Trending (sustained regimes) | 0.596 | 0.422 | stop wins | stop wins ✔ |
| Mean-reverting (dips snap back) | 0.207 | 0.428 | stop loses | stop loses ✔ |

The harness banks the edge where stops genuinely help (trending) and correctly fails to
where they whipsaw (mean-reverting) — the Kaminski-Lo split, in a bottle. (Synthetic Sharpes
are a positive control for the pipeline, never market evidence for a stamp.)

## Reproduce

```bash
python examples/verify.py               # real tape (this doc)
python examples/run_synthetic_demo.py   # offline trending vs mean-reverting controls
```
